initial_scene: The front-facing seated humanoid has a barrel-and-T-handle pump lying horizontally on the table. The silver barrel lies beside a black square mat; its long exposed plunger shaft extends toward image-right. The robot right hand is image-left, black-backed; robot left hand is image-right, white-backed.

observed_sequence.action: The robot right arm extends from its resting position toward the pump barrel; the left hand stays near the lap.
The right hand lowers over the cylindrical barrel and closes around it. The long shaft and T-shaped handle remain extended across the tabletop.

The right hand lifts the pump, turning the shaft from downward-forward to a horizontal direction toward the robot left, and brings it in front of the lower torso. The left hand begins rising to meet the handle.

The right fingers retain their barrel grasp. The left hand rises open, with fingers extended and thumb upright, and approaches the T-shaped handle at the opposite end of the horizontal shaft; native frames 198 and 214 separate approach from initial contact.

The left hand presses the handle toward the barrel while the right hand keeps its barrel grasp and also moves the barrel inward toward the left hand. The hands converge. The shaft exposed between the barrel mouth and T-handle visibly shortens from native 214 through 228, 244, 258, 274, and 290. This is relative plunger motion, not merely rotation or translation of the whole pump. A closed left-finger handle grasp is not demonstrated.

After the inward stroke, the left hand disengages by moving away from the handle with extended fingers (native 304); the right fingers retain the barrel grasp. The right hand alone then carries the pump toward the black mat. No hand-to-hand transfer occurs.
The right hand lowers the pump onto the black mat, leaving the cylindrical barrel lying on its side with much less exposed shaft than initially.

The right fingers open after the pump rests on the mat: native 388 shows hand still over the barrel, 400 shows visible separation, and 408 shows further withdrawal. Both arms settle by the lap and the released pump remains on the mat at final frame 463.

arm_hand_roles.right: Fingers close around the cylindrical barrel, bear the whole pump during pickup and transport, retain the barrel grasp during pressing, move the barrel inward toward the left hand during the stroke, then carry it back, place it on the mat and open to release.
arm_hand_roles.left: Initially near the lap, approaches the T-shaped plunger handle with largely extended fingers, presses the handle inward toward the barrel during the bimanual stroke, then moves away before the right-hand placement. A closed grasp around the handle is not established.
arm_hand_roles.coordination: Right hand bears and controls the barrel while left hand drives the plunger handle inward; both hands move toward one another during the stroke, reducing the barrel-to-handle distance. Left contact ends first, right barrel grasp persists through placement and release. No transfer or repeated outward-inward pumping cycle is shown.

anatomical_side_evidence.evidence: The initial PNG shows the robot head and chest front facing the camera, with both shoulder attachments visible. The image-left arm runs from the robot anatomical right shoulder to its black-backed hand. The image-right arm attaches to the anatomical left shoulder and ends in the white-backed hand. Native pickup and compression frames preserve these continuous arm attachments.

endpoint_evidence: The native final frame 463 shows the pump resting on the black mat independently of both withdrawn hands.
coverage: All four full-video contact sheets visually viewed again in the bimanual second review, covering every second decoded frame 0–462 (232 samples). Source initial PNG and 16 native pickup, bimanual-contact, mechanism, release and final PNGs visually viewed in this second pass.
terminal_state: The pump lies released on the black mat with the plunger visibly shortened; both hands have withdrawn to positions near the lap. No connected inflation target or externally visible pneumatic effect is shown.
selected_execution_status_basis: The visible barrel pickup, coordinated inward plunger stroke, return, and released placement all complete within the clip. Success refers to the observed mechanical manipulation rather than a measured pneumatic output.
uncertainties: Air pressure, airflow, and effective pneumatic compression cannot be verified visually; the review establishes a visible inward mechanical plunger stroke only.

The T-handle is partly occluded by the left fingers during pressing; exact individual finger contact and any hidden palm contact cannot be determined. The left hand is visibly largely open, so a closed handle grasp is not claimed.

The exact instant and depth of final plunger insertion are hidden between the hands; the shrinking exposed shaft and the shortened released pump establish inward relative motion, not measured full insertion.
annotation_discrepancies: The source wording describes rhythmic force application and effective air compression; the footage visibly supports a single inward plunger stroke, with no externally observable pneumatic output.
